title: 1957 AHSME Problem 17
statement: A cube is made by soldering twelve \(3\)-inch lengths of wire properly at the vertices of the cube. If a fly alights at one of the vertices and then walks along the edges, the greatest distance it could travel before coming to any vertex a second time, without retracing any distance, is:

solutions.text:
The cube has eight vertices. A path can visit all eight once, using seven edges, and then traverse the edge from its last vertex back to its starting vertex; the return is the first repeated vertex. Thus the greatest permitted walk uses eight edges. Its length is \(8\cdot3=24\) inches.

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: A path that never returns to a vertex can visit at most all eight cube vertices
Exhibit a path through all eight vertices, which uses seven edges before the next step returns to the starting vertex
